title: Introduce per-invocation bandwidth metrics and contextual log snapshotter
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Adds per-invocation bandwidth metrics (request/response bytes, embedding payload size, kv-cache-delta) and a sampled, scrubbed log snapshotter for high-bandwidth/failed invocations; new dashboard and alert rules for bandwidth SLOs; runtime hooks for tagging and trace enrichment.
description:
Motivation: We frequently surface latency/cost SLOs but lack a clear signal for invocation-level bandwidth (payload + generated bytes) which drives egress costs and can cause tail latency when responses are large. This PR introduces a compact per-invocation bandwidth allocator and a privacy-conscious sampled log snapshotter so SRE and product teams can correlate bandwidth spikes with model behavior and customer payloads without shipping PII to observability backends.

What this does (high level):
- Introduces metrics emitted per invocation: invocation.request_bytes, invocation.generated_bytes, invocation.total_bytes, invocation.kv_cache_delta_bytes. These are tagged by route, model_version, tenant_id (hashed), and warmup_tag.
- Adds a small allocator in the runtime that accounts for buffered chunks (streaming) to avoid double-counting while keeping memory overhead bounded. The allocator is careful to account for partial chunking and retries.
- Implements a sampled log snapshotter (reservoir sampler) that captures a scrubbed payload + truncated response for a configurable fraction of high-bandwidth or erroring invocations. Snapshots are PII-scrubbed using the existing prompt-sanitizer pipeline and optionally hashed for tenant correlation. Snapshots are emitted to the observability pipeline as compact JSON blobs with strict size caps.
- Adds an Invocation Bandwidth dashboard (observability/dashboards/invocation-bandwidth.json) showing per-route bytes distribution, 99/95/50 quantiles, bandwidth vs latency scatter, and example sampled snapshots linked by trace id.
- Adds alert rules for sustained bandwidth SLO breach: monitoring/alerts/bandwidth_slo.yaml. Policy: if 99th percentile of invocation.total_bytes exceeds configured threshold for 10m with increased rate of errors, trigger P1 runbook.
- Exposes an API toggle for tenants to opt out of snapshot collection; snapshot metadata (size, sampler_reason) is always recorded even when snapshots are disabled.

Why this is different from existing metrics: Many of our current observability changes focus on token or cost decomposition; bandwidth is orthogonal and necessary for egress cost attribution and for diagnosing slow tails caused by large outputs, streaming backpressure, or network stalls. The allocator prevents double-counting between streaming chunks and the final aggregation which avoided a ~30% overcount in our internal perf test.

Commits summary:
- feat(runtime): add invocation bandwidth allocator and metric hooks (5 commits merged into one)
- feat(obs): dashboard + alert rules for invocation bandwidth
- feat(logging): sampled log snapshotter with sanitizer integration and opt-out flag
- test: unit + integration tests for allocator accounting and sampler
- docs: developer notes and runbook updates for bandwidth SLOs

Files changed (high level):
- src/runtime/metrics/bandwidth_allocator.go - new allocator and accounting helpers
- src/runtime/metrics/bandwidth_test.go - unit tests for chunk accounting and retries
- src/runtime/tracing/trace_enricher.go - attach bandwidth tags to traces
- src/observability/dashboards/invocation-bandwidth.json - new dashboard panels and links to snapshots
- monitoring/alerts/bandwidth_slo.yaml - new alerting policy with runbook reference
- src/logging/snapshotter/reservoir_sampler.go - sampled snapshot implementation with sanitizer hook
- src/logging/snapshotter/snapshot_store.go - upload/size cap + encryption metadata
- pkg/config/feature_flags.go - tenant opt-out toggle and sampling config
- scripts/observability/seed_dashboards.sh - add dashboard to staging and prod orgs
- docs/runbooks/bandwidth_slo.md - runbook and triage steps

Review conversation (high level excerpts):
- Samir Patel (reviewer): "This looks reasonable. Two asks: 1) add e2e test with real streaming chunks + retry to ensure no double-counting; 2) make sure the default sampler rate is conservative for GA (0.1%). Also please add an opt-out in the tenant UI flows."
- Author (Anika): "Added integration test in bandwidth_integration_test.go that replays chunked responses with injected retry; sampler default lowered to 0.1% in config and opt-out flag exposed via tenant feature_flags. UI work tracked separately (ENG-5490)."
- Evelyn Chu (reviewer): "Privacy check: does snapshot sanitizer use the same regex/PII rules as request-logging? We must ensure no hashing errors leak variable-length secrets."
- Author (Anika): "Yes, snapshotter reuses the prompt-sanitizer pipeline (src/logging/sanitizer/). We added an additional post-scrub length cap and ensure deterministic hashing uses HKDF with tenant-scoped salt. See snapshot_store.go for details and unit tests covering edge cases."
- Diego Morales (approver): "CI initially failed on a flaky allocator test; fixed with a minor timing tolerance increase and deterministic RNG seed in the sampler test. Approving now."

CI:
- Checks run: unit-tests (linux), integration-tests (staging infra flap), lint, gosec, dashboard-validation.
- First run: unit-tests failed (allocator race), rerun after fix -> all checks pass.

Performance and cost notes:
- Microbenchmarks show allocator adds ~0.6% CPU on the hot path and ~1.4KB memory per concurrent streaming invocation under stress; metric emission is batched to reduce cardinality pressure.
- Snapshot uploads are capped to 8KB and use gzip; expected observability retention cost estimated at <0.02% of current logs spend at default sampler rate (0.1%).

Rollout plan:
1) Canary on staging and a subset of low-traffic tenants with snapshots disabled by default (config flag off).
2) Enable metrics only for all prod tenants (no snapshots) to populate dashboard and alert baselines.
3) Enable sampled snapshots for internal tenants and opt-in customers; monitor cost/PII metrics for one week.
4) Gradually increase sampler as needed after operations review.

Runbook pointers: docs/runbooks/bandwidth_slo.md includes triage steps, dashboards to examine, and remediation (throttle, model fallback to smaller variants, apply response truncation policy).

Merge: Squash-and-merge. Changelog message included (see release_notes).
